platforms.name: llama.cpp
platforms.notes: Backend table has no Gaudi/Habana entry. Tensor-parallel split mode is explicitly EXPERIMENTAL and unimplemented for most MoE/hybrid architectures (expert placement instead relies on manual --n-cpu-moe/--override-tensor flags). FP8 is not a first-class ggml dtype — it exists only as the internal scale format inside MXFP4/NVFP4 blocks. AWQ/GPTQ GGUF-conversion tooling was removed/never supported.

platforms.name: LMDeploy
platforms.notes: AMD is partial: a ROCm install path exists (LMDEPLOY_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm) but KV-cache quantization docs restrict to CUDA/Ascend and the internal device_type validator omits rocm. No CPU-only backend (device_type validator allows only cuda/ascend/maca/camb). Speculative decoding (EAGLE/EAGLE3) is explicitly labeled experimental. Also supports Moore Threads MACA and Cambricon NPU (outside this matrix's hardware keys).

platforms.name: MLX-LM
platforms.notes: MLX is no longer Apple-only: mlx core now ships an official CUDA backend for Linux/NVIDIA (pip install mlx[cuda12]) and a separate CPU-only Linux backend, alongside its original Metal/Apple-Silicon path — mlx-lm's own setup.py confirms this at the package level (extras_require cuda12/cuda13/cpu each pull in the matching mlx[...] backend, overriding the base install_requires' Darwin-only mlx dependency) — no AMD/Gaudi/Ascend backend exists in either repo. GGUF is export-only and limited to Mistral/Mixtral/Llama-style models (mlx-lm cannot load a .gguf file for inference). KV-cache quantization is integer/affine, not FP8-format.

platforms.name: Ollama
platforms.notes: Judged on Ollama's own documented behavior, not inherited llama.cpp capability. gpu.mdx (the dedicated hardware doc) covers only Nvidia/AMD-ROCm/Metal/Vulkan — no Ascend or Gaudi section. No tensor-parallel/split-mode flag is exposed; MoE expert-offload PRs are unmerged. Speculative decoding merged only on the Apple-Silicon MLX runner for specific models — the general feature request is still open. No hybrid state-space models in Ollama's library (Jamba/Mamba/Falcon-Mamba all 404 on ollama.com). nvfp4 downgraded to partial: import.mdx's own quantize docs list only q8_0/q4_K_S/q4_K_M, and NVFP4-tagged models exist on ollama.com/library (e.g. qwen3.6:27b-coding-nvfp4) but loading one hits an open, unresolved crash — issue #16056 reports `ggml.c:1676: GGML_ASSERT(type >= 0 && type < GGML_TYPE_COUNT) failed` loading an NVFP4 GGUF; the corresponding llama.cpp PR is linked but not yet ported to Ollama's fork.

platforms.name: SGLang
platforms.notes: intel_gaudi marked partial: no dedicated hardware-platform guide (overview.mdx lists only nvidia/amd/ascend/cpu/jetson/tpu/xpu), but --device accepts "hpu" and a legacy HpuCommunicator class exists (inherited from the vLLM lineage). gguf is NVIDIA+Ascend only — no AMD/ROCm (Marlin-kernel dependent).

platforms.name: TensorRT-LLM
platforms.notes: NVIDIA-only, proprietary TensorRT compiler stack — no AMD/Gaudi/ Apple/Ascend/CPU inference path in any fetched doc. Disaggregated serving is documented as mature but limited to decoder-only models at beam width 1. GGUF is never mentioned (TRT-LLM uses its own ModelOpt checkpoint/engine format).

platforms.name: Text Generation Inference (TGI)
platforms.notes: TGI is in maintenance mode as of this verification (README: only bug-fix/doc PRs accepted, recommends vLLM/SGLang/llama.cpp/MLX going forward). ep_size != 1 explicitly raises for DeepSeek-V2 (expert parallel unsupported); no pipeline-parallel or hybrid Mamba/Jamba model support found. AMD/ROCm does not support AWQ checkpoint loading.

platforms.name: vLLM
platforms.notes: Apple GPU support ships via the vllm-project-org vllm-metal plugin (MLX backend); Gaudi/Ascend likewise via official out-of-tree vllm-project plugins, not the in-tree core. GGUF requires the separate vllm-gguf-plugin. Disaggregated prefill is documented but the page itself is titled "experimental".

alerts.subject: Prompt Injection Vulnerability in Ollama, Gemma4 and HuggingFace's Transformers
alerts.what_happened: A community report describes a prompt injection vulnerability affecting Ollama, the Gemma4 model, and HuggingFace Transformers. Operators running these components in self-hosted inference stacks should review the report and validate untrusted input handling in their serving paths; the claim is from a Reddit post and has not been confirmed by a vendor advisory.

alerts.subject: A simple fix for LLM tail latency
alerts.what_happened: Engineering blog post describing a fix for tail latency in LLM serving, surfaced via an HN/vLLM feed. Relevant to operators tuning self-hosted inference request scheduling, but it is a single-team writeup rather than an upstream change — validate any suggested tuning against your own workload before adopting.

alerts.subject: Apple Silicon and macOS VMs: 11–16× Faster LLM Inference with Llama.cpp
alerts.what_happened: Blog post from the cua project documents GPU passthrough for macOS virtual machines on Apple Silicon, reporting 11-16x faster llama.cpp inference inside VMs compared to CPU-only virtualized execution. Relevant to operators running self-hosted inference on Apple Silicon hosts where VM isolation was previously a large performance penalty.

alerts.subject: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
alerts.what_happened: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters, is now available for local deployment via Ollama. It targets long-running agentic workloads with tool calling and multi-step task execution, and the low active-parameter count keeps inference cost lower than a dense 30B model on self-hosted GPUs.

alerts.subject: Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source
alerts.what_happened: Meta released Muse Glimmer, an open-source multimodal model family positioned for local and agentic use, published via the Hugging Face blog. Operators can evaluate the open weights for self-hosted serving, but should confirm the actual license terms, model sizes, and inference-runtime support (transformers/vLLM/llama.cpp) before planning a deployment.

alerts.subject: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
alerts.what_happened: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Glimmer, a 30B multimodal model under Apache 2.0 aimed at local coding agents, now pullable via Ollama. Ollama's MLX engine adds native DFlash and image input support for it, so Apple-silicon operators need a current Ollama build to run it; the permissive license allows on-prem deployment without usage restrictions.

alerts.subject: Announcing Day-0 Support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning on vLLM
alerts.what_happened: vLLM adds day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, serving it through OpenAI-compatible APIs with speculative decoding and both BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints. Operators running vLLM on NVIDIA GPUs or edge systems can deploy the model without waiting for a later release.

alerts.subject: vLLM Serving Experiments on H100s – config beats the baseline on p95 TTFT,ITL
alerts.what_happened: A write-up of vLLM serving experiments on H100 GPUs reports that tuning server configuration (scheduling/batching knobs) improved p95 time-to-first-token and inter-token latency versus the default baseline. Useful as a tuning reference for operators running vLLM on H100s; no software release or required action.

alerts.subject: LLM Scaler – LLM Support for Intel's Arc Pro B60 and B70 GPUs
alerts.what_happened: Intel published llm-scaler, an open-source stack that packages vLLM and supporting components (Docker images, driver/runtime setup, multi-GPU serving) for Arc Pro B60 and B70 GPUs. It gives operators a supported path to self-host open-weight LLM inference on Intel discrete GPUs instead of CUDA hardware; expect feature and model-coverage gaps versus the upstream CUDA path.

alerts.subject: Efficient Decode Context Parallelism with vLLM for Long Context Workloads
alerts.what_happened: vLLM added Decode Context Parallelism (DCP), which shards the KV cache across GPUs along the sequence dimension instead of replicating it as tensor parallelism does. The blog reports up to 3x higher throughput on long-context agentic workloads, making it worth evaluating for operators running long-context serving on multi-GPU nodes.

alerts.subject: LettuceDetect v2 in Semantic Router: Gen. Hallucination Detection vLLM Endpoint
alerts.what_happened: vLLM Semantic Router adds LettuceDetect v2, a generative hallucination-detection model served as a vLLM endpoint, allowing self-hosted deployments to flag unsupported claims in RAG/LLM responses at the routing layer. Optional to adopt; requires provisioning an additional model endpoint and GPU capacity alongside existing serving workloads.

alerts.subject: vLLM Reaches 25K Total TPS/GPU on Qwen3.5
alerts.what_happened: vLLM reports 25K total tokens/sec per GPU serving Qwen3.5-397B-A17B in NVFP4 on GB200 NVL72 using disaggregated prefill/decode, Blackwell GDN kernels, HMA cache transfer, and async scheduling fixes. Operators on Blackwell-class hardware can adopt the published srt-slurm recipes; the gains do not apply to older GPU generations or non-NVFP4 checkpoints.
